chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn al-Hajjal, from Ahmad ibn Umar al-Halabi, from Abu Basir who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said to him: May I be sacrificed for you! I want to ask you a question — is there anyone here who would hear my words? He said: So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) raised a curtain between him and another room, looked into it, then said: O Abu Muhammad! Ask about whatever comes to you.

He said: I said: May I be sacrificed for you! Your Shia followers narrate that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) taught Ali (peace be upon him) a door (of knowledge) from which a thousand doors open for him. So he said: O Abu Muhammad! The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) taught Ali (peace be upon him) a thousand doors — from each door a thousand doors open. I said: This, by God, is the knowledge! He then made marks in the ground for a while, then said: It is a knowledge, but it is not that.

He then said: O Abu Muhammad! And with us is the Jami'a — and what do they know what the Jami'a is? I said: May I be sacrificed for you! And what is the Jami'a? He said: A parchment seventy cubits long by the cubit of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), dictated from his own mouth and written by Ali's right hand. In it is every permissible and forbidden thing, and everything the people need, to the extent of the blood-money for a scratch. He then extended his hand toward me and said: Do you permit me, O Abu Muhammad? I said: May I be sacrificed for you! I am but yours — do whatever you wish. So he pressed me with his hand and said: To the extent of this — as if he were angry. I said: This, by God, is the knowledge! He said: It is a knowledge, but it is not that.

Then he was silent for a while, then said: And with us is the Jafr — and what do they know what the Jafr is? I said: And what is the Jafr? He said: A leather vessel containing the knowledge of the prophets, the successors, and the scholars who have passed from the Children of Israel. I said: This is the knowledge! He said: It is a knowledge, but it is not that.

Then he was silent for a while, then said: And with us is the Parchment of Fatima (peace be upon her) — and what do they know what the Parchment of Fatima is? I said: And what is the Parchment of Fatima (peace be upon her)? He said: A parchment with three times the size of your Quran. By God! There is not a single letter from your Quran in it. I said: This, by God, is the knowledge! He said: It is a knowledge, but it is not that.

Then he was silent for a while, then said: With us is the knowledge of what has been and the knowledge of what will be until the Hour is established. I said: May I be sacrificed for you! This, by God, is the knowledge! He said: It is a knowledge, but it is not that.
He said: I said: May I be sacrificed for you! So what is the knowledge? He said: What newly occurs by night and by day — matter after matter and thing after thing — until the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.الأرش في الخدش: Blood-money for a scratch — indicating the Jami'a contains even the most minute legal rulings
key_terms.الجامعة: Al-Jami'a: A comprehensive parchment dictated by the Prophet and written by Imam Ali, containing all legal rulings
key_terms.الجفر: Al-Jafr: A leather vessel containing knowledge of the prophets, their successors, and the scholars of Bani Isra'il
key_terms.ما يحدث بالليل والنهار: What newly occurs by night and day — the continuously unfolding divine knowledge given to the Imams
key_terms.مصحف فاطمة: Mushaf Fatima: The Parchment of Lady Fatima, three times the size of the Quran but containing no Quranic text

ai.seo_question: What are the special books and repositories of knowledge possessed by the Shia Imams according to al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Abu Basir, a close companion of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), privately questions the Imam about the special repositories of knowledge possessed by the Imams. The Imam systematically describes four great sources — the thousand-door knowledge taught by the Prophet to Ali, the Jami'a (a comprehensive parchment of all legal rulings), the Jafr (a leather vessel with knowledge of prophets and successors), and the Mushaf Fatima (a parchment three times the size of the Quran) — yet declares each insufficient. In a climactic revelation, the Imam defines true Imamate knowledge as the divinely unfolding knowledge of events as they occur continuously through time, until the Day of Judgment.
